facts.statement: Nemacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish.
The name Nemacanthus means 'to distribute spine' and the genus belongs to the family Palaeospinacidae.
facts.quote: Nemacanthus (from , 'to distribute' and , 'spine') is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish in the family Palaeospinacidae.

facts.statement: The genus Nemacanthus was described by Agassiz in 1837.
The oldest known fossils of Nemacanthus date to the Middle Permian period.
facts.quote: The geologically oldest records of Nemacanthus sp. date to the Middle Permian.

facts.statement: Fossils of Nemacanthus have been found in the Wordian age Khuff Formation of Oman.
facts.quote: This includes records of Nemacanthus sp. from the Wordian age Khuff Formation of Oman.

facts.statement: The species Nemacanthus elegans lived during the Triassic period in Idaho, United States.
facts.quote: The species N. elegans is from the Triassic of Idaho, United States.

facts.statement: The genus Nemacanthus existed from the Wordian to the Toarcian, spanning 266.9 to 174.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Wordian to Toarcian (266.9 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Nemacanthus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
There are 83 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Nemacanthus.
